page: Amazon Web Services x8g.4xlarge is an ARM64-based, memory-optimized server powered by AWS Neoverse-V2 processors running at 2.8 GHz. It features 16 dedicated physical cores with single-threaded execution and a cache hierarchy consisting of 64 KB L1d, 2 MB L2, and 36 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high resource density of 16.0 GB of RAM per core. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, lacks local storage, and provides an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark data indicates exceptional memory subsystem performance, with the Passmark memory score ranking in the top tier. Large-block uncached memory read and write bandwidths are strong, measuring 292.71 GB/sec and 124.24 GB/sec respectively. Database operations also perform strongly, placing in the top 25% of tested systems. However, compute-heavy tasks like single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests, as well as Redis SET operations, fall into the average category. The instance exhibits weak to poor performance in LLM inference tasks, particularly for text generation with small models and prompt processing with medium models.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and top-tier memory bandwidth, the x8g.4xlarge offers strong qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound applications that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. The absence of hyperthreading ensures predictable, dedicated core performance. This profile makes the server highly suitable for in-memory databases, caching layers, large-scale data processing, and memory-intensive enterprise workloads.
